title.narrative: Priority 3: Provision of Health (80%) and protection (20%) services to persons deprived of their liberty in Tripoli, Zgharta, Koura, Batroun, Bcharreh, Minieh-Danniyeh, and Akkar districts.

description.narrative:
ltpgtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="background-color: white color: black"gtThe conditions in places of detention in Lebanon are characterized by alarming and dire circumstances that significantly impact detainees’ dignity and human rights. Overcrowding, inadequate infrastructure, limited access to basic needs, poor hygiene conditions, and ill-treatment represent the primary challenges prevailing in places of detention. The lack of proper healthcare and mental health services further exacerbates the already distressing situation. Places of detention in Lebanon are grappling with severe overcrowding, ltbgtsurpassing their maximum occupancy rate by 323%lt/bgt. In North Lebanon, the prison population comprises ltbgt1,048 detaineeslt/bgt, with women accounting for 7% of the total. Among the prisoners, 70% are Lebanese, 23% are Syrian refugees, 4% are individuals of other nationalities, and 3% are stateless persons. Since 2005, Restart Center has been the sole health-focused national NGO providing health, mental health, and rehabilitation services in North Lebanon's prisons. In 2019, Restart Center’s services extended to 31 police stations, including remote detention facilities located in Akkar.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size: 14px background-color: white color: black"gtIn 2022, Restart Center has observed a concerning lt/spangtltb style="font-size: 14px color: black"gtrise in mortality and morbidity risks among detaineeslt/bgtltspan style="font-size: 14px background-color: white color: black"gt due to multiple factors. Limited access to primary, secondary, and tertiary medical care, exacerbated by a scarcity of healthcare professionals willing to work within detention facilities, further compounds the issue. Additionally, the absence of subsidized laboratory diagnostic tests, including those for infectious diseases, and a severe shortage of essential medications contribute to the precarious health conditions faced by detainees. In 2022 alone, 34 deaths were documented in places of detention in Lebanon. Furthermore, lt/spangtltb style="font-size: 14px color: black"gtthe right to a timely and fair trial process is not safeguardedlt/bgtltspan style="font-size: 14px background-color: white color: black"gt in northern Lebanon, where approximately ltbgt82% of detainees are pretrial inmates lt/bgtwho are still awaiting conviction.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size: 14px background-color: white color: black"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtltspan style="color: black background: white"gtThe proposed project aims to provideltbgt health (80%) and protection (20%) services to 800 vulnerablelt/bgt ltbgtLebanese, Syrian refugees, stateless persons, migrants, Palestinian refugees (PRS/PRL), and refugees of other nationalities, including 400 held in places of detention in northern Lebanon.lt/bgtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px color: black background: white"gt In particular, lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtthis project lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px color: black background: white"gtfalls under ltbgtpillar threelt/bgt of the LHF 2023 First Standard Allocation Strategy. It aims to lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtreduce risks associated with detention through regular detention monitoring and identification of the needs of vulnerable detainees, strengthening their access to legal aid, basic assistance, medical and protection services, and improving their detention conditions.lt/spangtltspan style="mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri mso-hansi-font-family:Calibrimso-bidi-font-family:Calibribackground:white"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="mso-ascii-font-family: Calibrimso-hansi-font-family:Calibrimso-bidi-font-family:Calibricolor:black mso-color-alt:windowtextbackground:white"gtSpecifically, the proposed project will contribute to improving the health, mental health, and legal situation and prison conditions of 400 vulnerable persons deprived of their liberty (of which 60% are Lebanese, 30% are Syrian refugees, and 10% are detainees of other nationalities) in 41 places of detention in North Lebanon and Akkar governorates, including seven prisons, 31 police stations, Tripoli palace of justice’s detention facility, Kobbeh military prison, the military police prison, and the Narcotic Control Bureau. The project will mainly target Tripoli, Zgharta, Koura, Batroun, Bcharreh, Minieh-Danniyeh, and Akkar districts where prisons and police stations are mainly located. lt/spangtltspan style="mso-ascii-font-family: Calibrimso-hansi-font-family:Calibrimso-bidi-font-family:Calibribackground: white"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify" class="MsoNormal"gtlta name="_Hlk135313518"gtltspan style="mso-ascii-font-family:Calibrimso-hansi-font-family:Calibrimso-bidi-font-family: Calibricolor:blackmso-color-alt:windowtextbackground:white"gtThe proposed project also includes a ltbgtlocalization componentlt/bgt. In particular, Restart Center will continue to support and build the capacity of “First Step Together Association” (FISTA) under this project. RESTART provided capacity development to FISTA under a previous LHF fund, particularly in the areas of financial management, human resources, and procurement. This was aimed at supporting the local NGO in expanding its funding opportunities and enhancing the quality of its services to persons with disabilities. Under the proposed project, Restart Center will focus on strengthening FISTA's capacity in key areas of project cycle management and Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning.lt/spangtlt/agtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltbrgtlt/pgt
